pr_title: feat(core): show warning when nested appRef.isStable() is triggered
pr_body:
Close #49275

When we call `ngZone.run()` inside `ApplicationRef.isStable` subscribe callback, it causes an endless loop, since `ngZone.run()` causes `isStable()` to be emitted again. This is by design, and this PR introduces a `console.warn` in `ngDevMode` to let the user know the possible cause.

issue_context.title: An endless call when run zone.run in ApplicationRef.isStable
comments:
The example you mention [works for me](https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ztrmsu?file=src%2Fmain.ts).

Calling `NgZone.run` unconditionally from `isStable` is definitely an infinite loop - `NgZone.run` adds a task to the zone, making it unstable and then stable again, which will run the `subscribe` callback again, which runs `NgZone.run` again, etc. This behavior is expected, and the examples don't suggest to me that it would behave otherwise.

I agree with you, and I read [checkStable](https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/e1355e7d16337177866cc1f8654b76381f26dae3/packages/core/src/zone/ng_zone.ts#L322) in ngZone which has the same hidden peril like this.

Maybe Angular could stop applying the stable observable or export a piped observable with `first` operation with rxjs.

Hi @JiaLiPassion 

I’ve saw your MR with moving the `zone._nesting--;`. But in your fix, the endless-call problem is only eliminated in `NgZone`. I have tried to run ngzone.run in the subscription of `NgZone.onStable`, the endless-call gone.

But, when i run ngzone.run in the subscription of `ApplicationRef.isStable`, the endless-call is still there. So I think it should fixed by both NgZone and ApplicationRef.

And Hi @alxhub @atscott 

I hope u can reevaluate this issue please.

- Make 2 PR to follow NgZone and ApplicationRef situation
- It's not only a doc problem, i think `label: core` could be added at least.
- Raise P5 to P4 or above

Thx!
